written: before any measurement of this track; never edited after a run. A change is a new revision file with its reason, and the verdict stays under the revision it was run with.
question: Does splitting one multi-question request (N questions sharing one context) across the Neural Engine (B=1 fixed-shape Core ML artifacts, rows one after another) and the MLX GPU (one batch), both at once, answer it faster than today's GPU-only path and than laya-fast on this machine, without changing any decision and without making the single-question P99 of the product mixes worse?

policy.name: makespan split
policy.applies_to: requests with 2 or more questions, Laya(device="auto", execution="workers"); 1-question requests are never touched
policy.eligible_row: some loaded ANE bucket fits it (length <= bucket, options <= 32)
policy.ane_rows: the k longest eligible rows, run one after another at B=1 as one ANE job
policy.gpu_rows: the rest, as one MLX batch job
policy.choice_of_k: argmin over k = 0..eligible of max(ane_backlog + sum ane_ms(bucket), gpu_backlog + gpu_ms(longest GPU row, GPU rows)); a side with no rows costs 0; ties go to the smaller k
policy.service_model: laya_apple.scheduling.ServiceModel of the instance (the shipped routing.json forward P50s on this profile); backlogs read once from the product's device queues
policy.buckets_loaded: the model's auto buckets plus the bucket each workload's longest row needs (64, 128, 512); the auto tie band pinned to laya-apple 1.5.0's
policy.fallback: none: a device error fails the request

workloads.definition: laya_apple.workload.make_request(tokenizer, config, tokens, n_questions, seed): the longest prompt row is exactly `tokens` long; questions cycle through QUESTION_POOL

arms.gpu: Laya.submit, unchanged (laya-apple 1.5 routes every one of these requests to the GPU)
arms.ane: every row as one ANE job on the product's ANE worker (report only)
arms.laya_fast: laya-fast at the pinned commit, unmodified, through LayaFast(model_dir).system_one (8x512 on laya only)

latency.arm_order: within a workload, ARMS rotated by (cycle + workload index) mod 3; workloads in the fixed order 8x128, 8x512, 1x512, 32x64
latency.boundary: caller-observed: from the call that submits the request (before tokenisation) until its answers are in the calling thread; the same for laya-fast (system_one call to return)
latency.window_statistic: P50 of the window's measured requests

laya_fast.location: a throwaway checkout and venv under ~/Developer/scratch/v16/laya-fast, removed after the campaign
laya_fast.install: uv venv --python 3.12; uv pip install -r requirements-lock.txt, then -r requirements-export.txt (its README's two steps); the installed versions are recorded
laya_fast.checkpoint: convaiinnovations/laya at 1c5edc17a7acd8701df6fc341c0d179f1c62c982 (its README's revision), converted with its convert.py --dtype float16; model.safetensors must hash to laya-apple's pinned 891102d372688fc2a094dac56a384bc537b87c63f21f9f3dac0be2b7cbc8d86c

blocks.pairing: each ours run with the adjacent lf run of its block (design.adjacent_pairs); window pairs are the two runs' 8x512 windows of the same cycle

protocol.machine: Apple M4 Max, the release profile; exclusive; AC power; the local LLM server and every other GPU/ANE consumer stopped; Core ML E5 cache not cleared; LAYA_APPLE_CACHE and HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 set

switchyard.workload: switchyard-v1 timetable and payloads (laya_apple.demos.switchyard.world.schedule / warmup_schedule, driver.payloads), standard seed and duration

serve.note: benchmarks/serve's decision timetable and requests (scripts/bench_serve.client_schedule, build_requests), in process, no HTTP, no LLM

gates.statistic: per pair, the ratio candidate / reference of the pair's window statistic; the geometric mean of the ratios with a Student-t interval on the log ratios (df = n - 1), back-transformed (research/coreml-prebind-predict/scripts/gate.py, t_interval); a seeded percentile bootstrap is reported as sensitivity only

G2_against_todays_gpu_path.metric: window P50, split / gpu, pairs = the same run and cycle
G2_against_todays_gpu_path.combine: PASS if every part passes, FAIL if any fails, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE

G3_correctness.reference: PyTorch CPU FP32 (laya_apple.conversion.torch_reference) per fixture request, raw/reference-<model>.json; for the mixes, the same instance's idle Laya.submit answer of each multi-question payload
G3_correctness.scope: every split answer: the correctness pass and every measured request of every latency run, and every multi-question answer of every split round of both mixes
G3_correctness.shared_exceedance: a probability or action error above 0.02 on a fixture request where today's gpu arm also exceeds 0.02 makes G3 INCONCLUSIVE (not FAIL) and is reported as a finding about the product; any other exceedance or any hard mismatch is FAIL
G3_correctness.report_only: the gpu and ane arms' checks against the same reference

G4a_switchyard_mix.metric: per round, P99 of train latency (completion - scheduled arrival); pairs = adjacent split/base rounds of a block
G4a_switchyard_mix.PASS: 95% upper bound of split/base <= 1.05, and split late trains (> 100 ms) in total <= base late trains in total, and split oracle-wrong trains in total <= base's
G4a_switchyard_mix.FAIL: 95% lower bound > 1.05, or more late or oracle-wrong trains than base

G4b_serve_mix.metric: per round, P99 of short_1q latency (completion - scheduled arrival); pairs as G4a

validity.gpu_arm_on_gpu: every gpu-arm request answered on the GPU with reason multiple_questions (1x512: sequence_exceeds_ane_auto_range)
validity.ane_ready: each run's instance has the ANE ready and the needed buckets loaded; otherwise the run aborts (no fallback is measured)
validity.laya_fast_bodies: each laya-fast run loaded its 512 body; laya-fast's Python sources unmodified at the pinned commit
validity.mix_lag: open-loop client lag P99 <= 5 ms in every measured round (benchmarks/serve V1); a round above it is invalid
validity.crashes: a crashed run is re-run once in the same position; a second crash stops the campaign

sequence_and_fast_fail.F0: Before any timed run: fixtures, references, then the first latency run's correctness pass. Any split hard mismatch, or a non-shared error above 0.02: STOP, FAIL.
sequence_and_fast_fail.F1: After block 1 (10 pairs per gate): 99% t-intervals. STOP with FAIL if G1's lower bound >= 1.00, or G2 no-regression's lower bound > 1.05 on any workload, or G2 gain's lower bound >= 1.00, or any G3 failure. Otherwise continue. Never PASS here.
sequence_and_fast_fail.F2: After block 2 (20 pairs): the gates at 95%. G1, G2 and G3 must all PASS for the mixes to run. INCONCLUSIVE stops the campaign; there is no automatic extension.
sequence_and_fast_fail.F3: Mixes: switchyard first, then serve. Each stops itself after its block 1 if both pairs' ratios exceed 1.20 (FAIL). A FAIL in switchyard skips serve.
sequence_and_fast_fail.verdict: PASS if G1, G2, G3, G4a and G4b all PASS; FAIL if any FAILs; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. Throughput, latency and correctness are reported separately; no dimension is hidden in the verdict.

phase_b.design: 4 latency.py runs per model (no laya-fast), gates G2 and G3 per model, 20 pairs; F0 and F1 apply per model
phase_b.meaning: a model whose Phase B verdict is not PASS keeps today's GPU-only path for multi-question requests in any production change

promotion: A PASS is not a product change. The split is rebuilt with tests in laya_apple/scheduling.py in its own pull request, gated again by the real Switchyard campaign (benchmarks/switchyard/run.sh) and the serve campaign beside a local LLM (benchmarks/serve/run.sh, criteria-r2.json unchanged), each compared with the laya-apple 1.5 campaign re-run on the same machine.
